result.note: Tests the JPC referral of the FCRA Amendment Bill and its asset-control provisions under Section 14B and Chapter IIIA.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill as of August 2026:
items: In August 2026, the Lok Sabha referred the bill to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee.
The committee is due to submit its report in the first week of the Budget Session.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: The Lok Sabha referred the bill to a 31-member JPC on 12 August 2026, but the committee is due to report in the first week of the Winter Session, not the Budget Session. The bill, introduced in March, had drawn objections from Opposition parties and Christian civil society groups.
questions.source: On Wednesday, the Lok Sabha referred the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) amid Opposition protests.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the asset provisions under Section 14B and Chapter IIIA of the FCRA Amendment Bill referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee in August 2026:
items: A routine delay on the FCRA Online Portal can trigger automatic cessation of an NGO's certificate.
On cessation, a Designated Authority takes provisional control of the NGO's foreign contributions and assets, including assets funded only partly by them.
Places of worship covered by these provisions must retain their religious character.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. Without restored registration, the Designated Authority's control becomes permanent and it may transfer or sell the assets. Current rules already allow seizure on licence cancellation, and the bill extends this to expired registrations.
questions.source: That instantly hands a Designated Authority provisional control of an NGO's foreign contributions and assets, including those funded only partly by them.
